The daily field guide for digital media

AI Media Scout

2026-11-22 · All platforms · Open-source software

The edition has 100 complete guides and 13 screened discoveries. It completes 23 earlier pending guides and details 7 substantive release updates. Today’s source reviews cover Kilnframe’s FilmCraft integration and Clio’s on-device FilmCraft and Whisper workflow on Android. Other guides span animated dialogue, editable stem and MIDI handoffs, and learned material capture. Models and OS requirements vary by workflow. Code grants were read in full. Models, services, creative inputs and hardware or software hosts have separate requirements. This edition is based on source review and published documentation. No discovered app was installed or run. The expanded plan covered 120 fields, 1378/1378 repository-query attempts and 37 model tasks. The repository lane recorded 1378 successful, 0 partial and 0 failed queries, with 254 bounded. The model lane recorded 0 failed tasks. Metadata from 2,864 saved repository pages included 84,512 numeric identities. The complete retained backlog spans 120,138 candidates, including pilot history and 1,080 previously screened guides still pending before this edition. Creative relevance and the complete software grant were checked before including any discovery. Unreviewed and excluded records stay in local research. Live primary research yielded 800 complete usable responses from 1022 distinct URL attempts, including a non-GitHub source in each of 120 fields. 14 captures reached the size bound and 208 other sources were inaccessible or unusable. The ecosystem checks cover all 8 configured groups and record available findings and gaps. Evidence labels in this edition are 0 Recommended, 0 Ready to try, 100 Quality unverified, 13 Experimental. Repository searches returned no saved rows for Camera-reactive projection installations, Live production accessibility and routed captions, Learned material capture and de-lighting, Learned projector compensation and exhibit color. Primary web research for these fields is included in the coverage notes. Updated evidence labels for previous entries: Hologram Parallax Photo Studio (Experimental to Quality unverified), Arm Compute Flow Bricks (Quality unverified to Experimental). 33 model tasks reached the configured response limit of 50 rows. A model record remains a discovery lead until code and use are verified. Model tasks with no rows: text2text-generation, zero-shot-audio-classification, audio-segmentation, image-matting. The separate watchlist made 67 unsuccessful repository checks. Collection logged 5 enrichment failures. Credential-shaped material in unsealed captures was removed before sealing. The affected source origins and before-and-after hashes remain in private evidence.

Search and review counts

120 creative fields; 1378/1378 repository queries attempted; 37/37 model-task queries attempted. 85396 distinct source candidates and 1489 model leads. 100 detailed profiles and 13 additional screened discoveries. Source gaps: 0 failed repository queries, 0 partial repository queries, 254 bounded repository queries, 0 failed model-task queries and 0 web ecosystem gaps. Raw search candidates include duplicates of known tools, excluded projects and projects awaiting review; they are not verified recommendations.

Profiles are based on current primary documentation. Creative quality and performance claims are attributed to the developers unless hands-on testing is explicitly recorded. Unknown hardware requirements stay unknown. Code, model weights, hosted services, and required proprietary hosts can have different terms.

How it uses AI

TranslatedSubs uses speech models to draft timed captions and a CPU CTranslate2 route for English-to-Simplified Chinese translation. Optional translation and TTS providers are configurable. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Introduction

TranslatedSubs uses speech models to draft timed captions and a CPU CTranslate2 route for English-to-Simplified Chinese translation. Optional translation and TTS providers are configurable. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

What it is good for

Create draft Simplified Chinese subtitles for a short English clip and compare both text and timecodes before export. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Demo & examples

The project documents an offline INT8 conversion and smoke-test path for the local translation model, and shows the browser editor and project workflow. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

  1. Prepare source deployment using the documented Python and FFmpeg setup. Use FFmpeg with libass where the caption-rendering path requires it.
  2. Select the required speech model, add the optional local-translation dependencies and convert the documented English-to-Chinese model.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

  1. Import an authorized clip and draft time-aligned captions with the selected speech model.
  2. Translate the track locally, then revise names and specialized vocabulary line by line.
  3. Compare the cue duration and translated text against the source audio and review the exported subtitle format.

Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Hardware
Minimum RAM, VRAM and disk space for the scoped workflow are undocumented.
Software
Python 3.10–3.12, uv and appropriate FFmpeg, a speech model, and the CTranslate2 conversion package for the local translation route.
Platforms
The source browser workbench has Windows and macOS instructions, plus a separate Linux quick start. The native Apple silicon desktop build is pending acceptance and signing.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Dependencies and creative assets carry their own terms. [2] [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

  • Weights: MIT covers TranslatedSubs. Model weights, optional speech voices, cloud services and media inputs have their own grants. The local model documentation names the exact translation model to check.
  • Commercial: Project code is governed by MIT. Confirm selected model, source-media and output restrictions separately.
  • Cost: The scoped translation runs on CPU after model preparation. Optional hosted services and different speech or voice models may require additional fees.

Why it merits attention

The creative workflow is grounded in the cited documentation. Output quality and compatibility are not hands-on verified. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

Limitations

The local route is specifically English into Simplified Chinese. The displayed native desktop path is under development. Quantitative translation and subtitle timing accuracy remain unverified here. [1] [4] [5] [6] [7]

How it uses AI

Allosaurus is a pretrained multilingual phone recognizer for a WAV file or folder. It can return estimated time intervals in addition to phones. [1] [4] [5] [6]

Introduction

Allosaurus is a pretrained multilingual phone recognizer for a WAV file or folder. It can return estimated time intervals in addition to phones. [1] [4] [5] [6]

What it is good for

Draft phoneme timing from a recorded line for a manually designed character’s mouth-shape mapping. [1] [4] [5] [6]

Demo & examples

The official examples show sample speech decoded as a phone sequence and the optional timestamp mode. The Parrot Lipsync project is a separate first-party integration reference. [1] [4] [5] [6]

Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [1] [4] [5] [6]

  1. Use the project’s documented Python package route and select the supported pretrained model.
  2. Check the language’s phone inventory and prepare source dialogue as WAV.

First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [1] [4] [5] [6]

  1. Decode a short line with timestamps and review uncertain consonants and pauses next to the source audio.
  2. Map the resulting phones to the mouth-shape set intended for the selected character and language.
  3. Correct timings in the downstream timeline and keep the measured source and resulting cues for comparison.

Minimum RAM, VRAM and disk space for the scoped workflow are undocumented.

Allosaurus Python package and pretrained model, plus your target mouth-cue mapping workflow. The app supports selecting a device for inference.

Python application and library. Per-OS compatibility and minimum supported runtime versions are undocumented in the current overview.
